answer: At the start of each epoch, every agent posts a refundable bond before drawing a task from a common pool; a pulse of fresh identities therefore ties up capital one account at a time. Random audits compare signed task histories, and an echo of near-identical submissions triggers slashing. Honest agents recover their stake after review, but an attacker pays the bond for every Sybil and loses it on detected duplicates—making a seemingly free oasis of accounts expensive to sustain.
